title: 5.5.9 Playtest and reflect: Snake
description: Play your game at least three times, find one thing that surprised you, link it to your code and choose one change. AI-graded with hints.

aiGrader.prompt:
Everything you need is in 5.5.1 (Plan: Break Snake into parts) and 5.5.8 (Lab: Don't bite yourself): go back and reread them if you get stuck. A few short sentences per answer is plenty, in your own everyday words.

Play your finished Snake at least three times, trying to lose in different ways. Then answer:

1. How many rounds did you play, and how did they go?

2. What is one thing that surprised you or did not work as you expected?

3. Which part of your code do you think that comes from?

4. What is one rule or number you would change, and what would it do to the game?

rubric.title: Says how many rounds they played and how it went
rubric.description: The student says they played the finished game at least three times, or gives some concrete detail from their rounds (a score, a way they lost, how long the snake got). Credit any answer that shows they actually played. Only an answer with no sign of play is a miss.

rubric.title: Names one thing that surprised or broke
rubric.description: The student names one thing that did not work as they expected, a bug or a rough moment, and describes it concretely enough that another person could look for it (what they did, what happened). If they found nothing, a specific thing they checked and found fine is acceptable as partial.

rubric.title: Says which part of the code that touches
rubric.description: The student connects what they saw to a part of the game or its code, such as the beat, the tail removal, the isBody search or the food placement, even loosely. Any plausible link counts; they do not have to be right about the cause.

rubric.title: Names one rule they would change and what it would do
rubric.description: The student names one rule or number they would change (the speed, the grid size, wrapping at the walls, a bonus food) and says what the change would do to the game. Any specific change with an effect is full credit.
